The projector decomposition gives the exact repulsive-entry two-exponential formula. The row-sum identity proves the exact l-infinity norm, while explicit derivative and Taylor/spectral-gap expansions prove both endpoint laws. Exact-rational sample identities and an independently evaluated matrix exponential were replayed using the standalone checker; finite tests supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: One negative edge on a three-vertex positive path is the smallest nontrivial repulsive consensus loop, with a natural effective-resistance stability boundary. The theorem quantifies the full positivity-recovery and contractivity period rather than only the existence of eventual positivity. The critical separation between inverse-margin positivity delay and logarithmic peak time, with a nonvanishing limiting amplitude, supplies a concrete parameter-sharp robustness benchmark. The small-repulsion law is complementary and derived from the same natural parameter family.
